details:
This is a moon-buggy style game. It focuses on the equipment sent by NASA to Mars to collect data with the focus of educating school-age space enthusiasts in a fun way.

The game consists of five levels, each having a rover sent to Mars, in this specific order: Curiosity, Perseverance, Opportunity, Insight, and Ingenuity. The challenge is that the player will have maximum 3 hearts in each level in which you have to collect 6 parts, all while dodging hazards. Each part gives the rover a speed boost and shows what it does as it is collected. On collecting all 6 parts, the level and rover is upgraded. After each level, a report is shown that states why and when the rover was sent, in which region of Mars it landed, what it found, how it is doing now or how it stopped.

The game gets progressively harder after each level. The hazards match what really ended a mission, for example, dust-storm, a rough landing. After completing all 5 levels, a timeline of 11 machines sent to Mars (6 which are not included in the game) is shown , including the ones that the player built in the game.

We figured that almost every kid has an interest in space technology, however that interest is not strong enough to read through all the NASA mission pages. They have a short attention-span and you need something really addictive to keep them indulged. So we made Mars Buggy- the first 2 levels are easy, but when you pass on to the Quiet Ridge, the difficulty level becomes twice. On the first few tries, you will not even know what hit you. Then kicks in that psychological urge to win, pushing the kid to try again and again until he succeeds. That feeling of accomplishment finally makes him stop and read the environmental description of his hard-won rover.

This code contains HTML, JavaScript and CSS.
